#!/usr/bin/perl

use strict;
use warnings;
use IPC::Open2;

# An example hook script to integrate Watchman
# (https://facebook.github.io/watchman/) with git to speed up detecting
# new and modified files.
#
# The hook is passed a version (currently 2) and last update token
# formatted as a string and outputs to stdout a new update token and
# all files that have been modified since the update token. Paths must
# be relative to the root of the working tree and separated by a single NUL.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "query-watchman" and set
# 'git config core.fsmonitor .git/hooks/query-watchman'
#
my ($version, $last_update_token) = @ARGV;

# Uncomment for debugging
# print STDERR "$0 $version $last_update_token\n";

# Check the hook interface version
if ($version ne 2) {
	die "Unsupported query-fsmonitor hook version '$version'.\n" .
	    "Falling back to scanning...\n";
}

my $git_work_tree = get_working_dir();

my $retry = 1;

my $json_pkg;
eval {
	require JSON::XS;
	$json_pkg = "JSON::XS";
	1;
} or do {
	require JSON::PP;
	$json_pkg = "JSON::PP";
};

launch_watchman();

sub launch_watchman {
	my $o = watchman_query();
	if (is_work_tree_watched($o)) {
		output_result($o->{clock}, @{$o->{files}});
	}
}

sub output_result {
	my ($clockid, @files) = @_;

	# Uncomment for debugging watchman output
	# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-output.out");
	# binmode $fh, ":utf8";
	# print $fh "$clockid\n@files\n";
	# close $fh;

	binmode STDOUT, ":utf8";
	print $clockid;
	print "\0";
	local $, = "\0";
	print @files;
}

sub watchman_clock {
	my $response = qx/watchman clock "$git_work_tree"/;
	die "Failed to get clock id on '$git_work_tree'.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $? != 0;

	return $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
}

sub watchman_query {
	my $pid = open2(\*CHLD_OUT, \*CHLD_IN, 'watchman -j --no-pretty')
	or die "open2() failed: $!\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n";

	# In the query expression below we're asking for names of files that
	# changed since $last_update_token but not from the .git folder.
	#
	# To accomplish this, we're using the "since" generator to use the
	# recency index to select candidate nodes and "fields" to limit the
	# output to file names only. Then we're using the "expression" term to
	# further constrain the results.
	my $last_update_line = "";
	if (substr($last_update_token, 0, 1) eq "c") {
		$last_update_token = "\"$last_update_token\"";
		$last_update_line = qq[\n"since": $last_update_token,];
	}
	my $query = <<"	END";
		["query", "$git_work_tree", {$last_update_line
			"fields": ["name"],
			"expression": ["not", ["dirname", ".git"]]
		}]
	END

	# Uncomment for debugging the watchman query
	# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-query.json");
	# print $fh $query;
	# close $fh;

	print CHLD_IN $query;
	close CHLD_IN;
	my $response = do {local $/; <CHLD_OUT>};

	# Uncomment for debugging the watch response
	# open ($fh, ">", ".git/watchman-response.json");
	# print $fh $response;
	# close $fh;

	die "Watchman: command returned no output.\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $response eq "";
	die "Watchman: command returned invalid output: $response\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" unless $response =~ /^\{/;

	return $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
}

sub is_work_tree_watched {
	my ($output) = @_;
	my $error = $output->{error};
	if ($retry > 0 and $error and $error =~ m/unable to resolve root .* directory (.*) is not watched/) {
		$retry--;
		my $response = qx/watchman watch "$git_work_tree"/;
		die "Failed to make watchman watch '$git_work_tree'.\n" .
		    "Falling back to scanning...\n" if $? != 0;
		$output = $json_pkg->new->utf8->decode($response);
		$error = $output->{error};
		die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

		# Uncomment for debugging watchman output
		# open (my $fh, ">", ".git/watchman-output.out");
		# close $fh;

		# Watchman will always return all files on the first query so
		# return the fast "everything is dirty" flag to git and do the
		# Watchman query just to get it over with now so we won't pay
		# the cost in git to look up each individual file.
		my $o = watchman_clock();
		$error = $output->{error};

		die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
		"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

		output_result($o->{clock}, ("/"));
		$last_update_token = $o->{clock};

		eval { launch_watchman() };
		return 0;
	}

	die "Watchman: $error.\n" .
	"Falling back to scanning...\n" if $error;

	return 1;
}

sub get_working_dir {
	my $working_dir;
	if ($^O =~ 'msys' || $^O =~ 'cygwin') {
		$working_dir = Win32::GetCwd();
		$working_dir =~ tr/\\/\//;
	} else {
		require Cwd;
		$working_dir = Cwd::cwd();
	}

	return $working_dir;
}

#!/bin/sh
#
# An example hook script to verify what is about to be committed.
# Called by "git commit" with no arguments.  The hook should
# exit with non-zero status after issuing an appropriate message if
# it wants to stop the commit.
#
# To enable this hook, rename this file to "pre-commit".

if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1
then
	against=HEAD
else
	# Initial commit: diff against an empty tree object
	against=$(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)
fi

# If you want to allow non-ASCII filenames set this variable to true.
allownonascii=$(git config --type=bool hooks.allownonascii)

# Redirect output to stderr.
exec 1>&2

# Cross platform projects tend to avoid non-ASCII filenames; prevent
# them from being added to the repository. We exploit the fact that the
# printable range starts at the space character and ends with tilde.
if [ "$allownonascii" != "true" ] &&
	# Note that the use of brackets around a tr range is ok here, (it's
	# even required, for portability to Solaris 10's /usr/bin/tr), since
	# the square bracket bytes happen to fall in the designated range.
	test $(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=A -z $against |
	  LC_ALL=C tr -d '[ -~]\0' | wc -c) != 0
then
	cat <<\EOF
Error: Attempt to add a non-ASCII file name.

This can cause problems if you want to work with people on other platforms.

To be portable it is advisable to rename the file.

If you know what you are doing you can disable this check using:

  git config hooks.allownonascii true
EOF
	exit 1
fi

# If there are whitespace errors, print the offending file names and fail.
exec git diff-index --check --cached $against --

#!/bin/sh

# An example hook script to verify what is about to be pushed.  Called by "git
# push" after it has checked the remote status, but before anything has been
# pushed.  If this script exits with a non-zero status nothing will be pushed.
#
# This hook is called with the following parameters:
#
# $1 -- Name of the remote to which the push is being done
# $2 -- URL to which the push is being done
#
# If pushing without using a named remote those arguments will be equal.
#
# Information about the commits which are being pushed is supplied as lines to
# the standard input in the form:
#
#   <local ref> <local oid> <remote ref> <remote oid>
#
# This sample shows how to prevent push of commits where the log message starts
# with "WIP" (work in progress).

remote="$1"
url="$2"

zero=$(git hash-object --stdin </dev/null | tr '[0-9a-f]' '0')

while read local_ref local_oid remote_ref remote_oid
do
	if test "$local_oid" = "$zero"
	then
		# Handle delete
		:
	else
		if test "$remote_oid" = "$zero"
		then
			# New branch, examine all commits
			range="$local_oid"
		else
			# Update to existing branch, examine new commits
			range="$remote_oid..$local_oid"
		fi

		# Check for WIP commit
		commit=$(git rev-list -n 1 --grep '^WIP' "$range")
		if test -n "$commit"
		then
			echo >&2 "Found WIP commit in $local_ref, not pushing"
			exit 1
		fi
	fi
done

exit 0

This sample hook safeguards topic branches that have been
published from being rewound.

The workflow assumed here is:

 * Once a topic branch forks from "master", "master" is never
   merged into it again (either directly or indirectly).

 * Once a topic branch is fully cooked and merged into "master",
   it is deleted.  If you need to build on top of it to correct
   earlier mistakes, a new topic branch is created by forking at
   the tip of the "master".  This is not strictly necessary, but
   it makes it easier to keep your history simple.

 * Whenever you need to test or publish your changes to topic
   branches, merge them into "next" branch.

The script, being an example, hardcodes the publish branch name
to be "next", but it is trivial to make it configurable via
$GIT_DIR/config mechanism.

With this workflow, you would want to know:

(1) ... if a topic branch has ever been merged to "next".  Young
    topic branches can have stupid mistakes you would rather
    clean up before publishing, and things that have not been
    merged into other branches can be easily rebased without
    affecting other people.  But once it is published, you would
    not want to rewind it.

(2) ... if a topic branch has been fully merged to "master".
    Then you can delete it.  More importantly, you should not
    build on top of it -- other people may already want to
    change things related to the topic as patches against your
    "master", so if you need further changes, it is better to
    fork the topic (perhaps with the same name) afresh from the
    tip of "master".

Let's look at this example:

		   o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o "next"
		  /       /           /           /
		 /   a---a---b A     /           /
		/   /               /           /
	       /   /   c---c---c---c B         /
	      /   /   /             \         /
	     /   /   /   b---b C     \       /
	    /   /   /   /             \     /
    ---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o---o "master"


A, B and C are topic branches.

 * A has one fix since it was merged up to "next".

 * B has finished.  It has been fully merged up to "master" and "next",
   and is ready to be deleted.

 * C has not merged to "next" at all.

We would want to allow C to be rebased, refuse A, and encourage
B to be deleted.

To compute (1):

	git rev-list ^master ^topic next
	git rev-list ^master        next

	if these match, topic has not merged in next at all.

To compute (2):

	git rev-list master..topic

	if this is empty, it is fully merged to "master".

#!/bin/sh

# An example hook script to update a checked-out tree on a git push.
#
# This hook is invoked by git-receive-pack(1) when it reacts to git
# push and updates reference(s) in its repository, and when the push
# tries to update the branch that is currently checked out and the
# receive.denyCurrentBranch configuration variable is set to
# updateInstead.
#
# By default, such a push is refused if the working tree and the index
# of the remote repository has any difference from the currently
# checked out commit; when both the working tree and the index match
# the current commit, they are updated to match the newly pushed tip
# of the branch. This hook is to be used to override the default
# behaviour; however the code below reimplements the default behaviour
# as a starting point for convenient modification.
#
# The hook receives the commit with which the tip of the current
# branch is going to be updated:
commit=$1

# It can exit with a non-zero status to refuse the push (when it does
# so, it must not modify the index or the working tree).
die () {
	echo >&2 "$*"
	exit 1
}

# Or it can make any necessary changes to the working tree and to the
# index to bring them to the desired state when the tip of the current
# branch is updated to the new commit, and exit with a zero status.
#
# For example, the hook can simply run git read-tree -u -m HEAD "$1"
# in order to emulate git fetch that is run in the reverse direction
# with git push, as the two-tree form of git read-tree -u -m is
# essentially the same as git switch or git checkout that switches
# branches while keeping the local changes in the working tree that do
# not interfere with the difference between the branches.

# The below is a more-or-less exact translation to shell of the C code
# for the default behaviour for git's push-to-checkout hook defined in
# the push_to_deploy() function in builtin/receive-pack.c.
#
# Note that the hook will be executed from the repository directory,
# not from the working tree, so if you want to perform operations on
# the working tree, you will have to adapt your code accordingly, e.g.
# by adding "cd .." or using relative paths.

if ! git update-index -q --ignore-submodules --refresh
then
	die "Up-to-date check failed"
fi

if ! git diff-files --quiet --ignore-submodules --
then
	die "Working directory has unstaged changes"
fi

# This is a rough translation of:
#
#   head_has_history() ? "HEAD" : EMPTY_TREE_SHA1_HEX
if git cat-file -e HEAD 2>/dev/null
then
	head=HEAD
else
	head=$(git hash-object -t tree --stdin </dev/null)
fi

if ! git diff-index --quiet --cached --ignore-submodules $head --
then
	die "Working directory has staged changes"
fi

if ! git read-tree -u -m "$commit"
then
	die "Could not update working tree to new HEAD"
fi

pub fn parse_query(q: &str) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    let mut out: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> = vec![];
    for part in q.split('&') {
        if part.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = match part.split_once('=') {
            Some((k, v)) => (k, v),
            None => (part, ""),
        };
        let dec = |s: &str| percent_decode_str(&s.replace('+', " ")).decode_utf8_lossy().to_string();
        let (k, v) = (dec(k), dec(v));
        if let Some(e) = out.iter_mut().find(|(ek, _)| *ek == k) {
            e.1.push(v);
        } else {
            out.push((k, vec![v]));
        }
    }
    out
}

const RESTRICT_PARAM: &str = "output:only";

/// `EntityUtil.determineRestrictFields`
pub fn determine_restrict_fields(q: &[(String, Vec<String>)], restrictable: &[&str]) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let mut requested: Option<Vec<String>> = None;
    for (k, vals) in q {
        if k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(RESTRICT_PARAM) {
            let mut out = vec![];
            for v in vals {
                let mut parts: Vec<String> = split_commas(v);
                // Java's String.split drops trailing empty strings
                while parts.last().map(|s| s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(false) && parts.len() > 0 {
                    parts.pop();
                }
                if parts.is_empty() && v.is_empty() {
                    parts.push(String::new());
                }
                out.extend(parts);
            }
            requested = if out.is_empty() { None } else { Some(out) };
        }
    }
    let requested = requested?;
    let mut filtered = vec![];
    for r in restrictable {
        for req in &requested {
            if r.eq_ignore_ascii_case(req) {
                filtered.push(r.to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    if filtered.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(filtered)
    }
}

/// split at `\s*,\s*`
fn split_commas(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = vec![];
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == ',' {
            while cur.ends_with(|c: char| c.is_whitespace()) {
                cur.pop();
            }
            out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
            i += 1;
            while i < chars.len() && chars[i].is_whitespace() {
                i += 1;
            }
            continue;
        }
        if chars[i].is_whitespace() && cur.is_empty() && !out.is_empty() {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        cur.push(chars[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    out.push(cur);
    out
}

fn cast_value(prim: Prim, s: &str) -> B {
    match prim {
        Prim::Str => B::S(Some(s.to_string())),
        Prim::Int => B::I(Some(s.trim().parse::<i32>().unwrap_or(0))),
        Prim::Bool => {

            B::Bo(Some(matches!(l.as_str(), "true" | "yes" | "y" | "on" | "1")))
        }
        Prim::Dbl => B::D(Some(s.trim().parse::<f64>().ok().filter(|d| d.is_finite()).unwrap_or(0.0))),
    }
}

fn fix_user_groups(v: &mut Value, user_id: i32, ids: &[i32]) {

pub(crate) fn first_json_value(body: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Value>, ()> {
    let text = std::str::from_utf8(body).map_err(|_| ())?;
    if text.trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let mut it = serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(text).into_iter::<Value>();
    match it.next() {
        Some(Ok(v)) => Ok(Some(v)),
        _ => Err(()),
    }

fn as_int(v: &Value) -> i64 {
    match v {
        Value::Number(n) => n.as_i64().or_else(|| n.as_f64().map(|f| f as i64)).unwrap_or(0),
        Value::String(s) => {
            let t = s.trim();
            t.parse::<i64>().ok().or_else(|| t.parse::<f64>().ok().map(|f| f as i64)).unwrap_or(0)
        }
        Value::Bool(b) => *b as i64,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

            .bind(name)
            .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
            .await
            .ok()??;
        let id: i32 = row.get("id");
        let active: Option<bool> = row.get("active");
        if !active.unwrap_or(false) {
            return None;
        }
        let hash: Option<String> = row.get("password");
        let hash = hash?;
        if hash.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let pass = pass.to_string();
        let ok = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || bcrypt::verify(pass, &hash).unwrap_or(false))
            .await
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if !ok {
            return None;
        }
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "select r.name from users_roles ur join roles r on r.id = ur.role_id where ur.user_id = $1 \
             union \
             select r.name from user_usergroup ug join usergroups_roles gr on gr.usergroup_id = ug.usergroup_id \
             join roles r on r.id = gr.role_id where ug.user_id = $1",
        )
        .bind(id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .ok()?;
        let auth: HashSet<String> = rows.iter().filter_map(|r| r.get::<Option<String>, _>("name")).collect();
        if auth.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let admin = auth.contains(ROLE_ADMIN);
        Some((Principal { id, admin }, auth))
    }

    async fn perm_table(&self, p: &Principal) -> Result<PermTable, sqlx::Error> {
        let mut perms: HashMap<i32, HashSet<String>> = HashMap::new();
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "select up.entity_id, pp.permissions from userpermissions up \
             join permissioncollections_permissions pp on pp.permissioncollections_id = up.userpermissions_id \
             where up.userpermissions_key = $1",
        )
        .bind(p.id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        for r in rows {
            if let Some(s) = r.get::<Option<String>, _>("permissions") {
                perms.entry(r.get("entity_id")).or_default().insert(s);
            }
        }
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "select gp.entity_id, pp.permissions from grouppermissions gp \
             join user_usergroup ug on ug.usergroup_id = gp.grouppermissions_key \
             join permissioncollections_permissions pp on pp.permissioncollections_id = gp.grouppermissions_id \
             where ug.user_id = $1",
        )
        .bind(p.id)
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        for r in rows {
            if let Some(s) = r.get::<Option<String>, _>("permissions") {
                perms.entry(r.get("entity_id")).or_default().insert(s);
            }
        }
        let rows = sqlx::query("select usergroup_id from user_usergroup where user_id = $1")
            .bind(p.id)
            .fetch_all(&self.pool)
            .await?;
        let groups = rows.iter().map(|r| r.get::<i32, _>("usergroup_id")).collect();
        Ok(PermTable { perms, groups })
    }

    /// `hasRole(admin) or hasPermission(entity, perm)`
    fn allowed(&self, pt: &PermTable, p: &Principal, class: PClass, id: Option<i32>, perm: &str) -> bool {
        if p.admin {
            return true;
        }
        if perm == "READ" {
            match class {
                PClass::AlwaysRead => return true,
                PClass::User if id == Some(p.id) => return true,
                PClass::Group if id.map(|g| pt.groups.contains(&g)).unwrap_or(false) => return true,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        match id.and_then(|i| pt.perms.get(&i)) {
            Some(set) => set.contains(perm) || set.contains("ADMIN"),
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// GET / and GET /filter
    async fn list(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, query: &[(String, Vec<String>)], filter: bool) -> Reply {
        let fields = res.restrictable();
        let names: Vec<&str> = fields.iter().map(|f| f.0).collect();
        let restrict = determine_restrict_fields(query, &names);

        // filter conditions
        let mut conds: Vec<(usize, Vec<String>)> = vec![];
        if filter {
            for (fi, (fname, _, _)) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
                if let Some((_, vals)) = query
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|(k, _)| k != RESTRICT_PARAM)
                    .find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(fname))
                {
                    conds.push((fi, vals.clone()));
                }
            }
            if conds.is_empty() {
                return json_reply(200, &Value::Array(vec![]), true);
            }
        }
        let mut sql_where = String::new();
        let mut binds: Vec<B> = vec![];
        if !conds.is_empty() {
            let mut ands = vec![];
            for (fi, vals) in &conds {
                let (_, expr, prim) = fields[*fi];
                let mut ors = vec![];
                for v in vals {
                    binds.push(cast_value(prim, v));
                    ors.push(format!("{} = ${}", expr, binds.len()));
                }
                ands.push(format!("({})", ors.join(" or ")));
            }
            sql_where = format!(" where {}", ands.join(" and "));
        }
        let pt = if p.admin {
            None
        } else {
            match self.perm_table(p).await {
                Ok(t) => Some(t),
                Err(_) => return status(500),
            }
        };
        let kind = res.kind();
        let from = res.from_sql();
        let mut items: Vec<Value> = vec![];
        match restrict {
            Some(rf) => {
                if res == Res::DataSources {
                    // aliasToBean cannot instantiate the abstract entity
                    return status(500);
                }
                let sel: Vec<&(&str, &str, Prim)> = rf
                    .iter()
                    .filter_map(|n| fields.iter().find(|f| f.0 == n))
                    .collect();
                let cols: Vec<String> = sel.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, f)| format!("{} as c{}", f.1, i)).collect();
                let sql = format!("select {} from {}{} order by t.id", cols.join(", "), from, sql_where);
                let mut q = sqlx::query(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql));
                for b in binds {
                    q = match b {
                        B::I(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::S(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::D(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::Bo(v) => q.bind(v),
                    };
                }
                let rows = match q.fetch_all(&self.pool).await {
                    Ok(r) => r,
                    Err(_) => return status(500),
                };
                for r in rows {
                    let mut o = spec::new_instance(kind);
                    for (i, f) in sel.iter().enumerate() {
                        let col = format!("c{}", i);
                        let v: Value = match f.2 {
                            Prim::Str => r.get::<Option<String>, _>(col.as_str()).map(Value::String).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
                            Prim::Int => r.get::<Option<i32>, _>(col.as_str()).map(|x| x.into()).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
                            Prim::Bool => r.get::<Option<bool>, _>(col.as_str()).map(Value::Bool).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
                            Prim::Dbl => r.get::<Option<f64>, _>(col.as_str()).map(|x| x.into()).unwrap_or(Value::Null),
                        };
                        // primitives cannot hold null
                        let v = if v.is_null() && f.0 == "active" { Value::Bool(false) } else { v };
                        o.insert(f.0.to_string(), v);
                    }
                    // the partial entity carries no permissions: only types that
                    // everybody may read survive the post filter
                    let visible = match &pt {
                        None => true,
                        Some(t) => self.allowed(t, p, res.pclass(), None, "READ"),
                    };
                    if visible {
                        items.push(spec::serialize(kind, &o));
                    }
                }
            }
            None => {
                let sql = format!("select t.id from {}{} order by t.id", from, sql_where);
                let mut q = sqlx::query(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql));
                for b in binds {
                    q = match b {
                        B::I(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::S(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::D(v) => q.bind(v),
                        B::Bo(v) => q.bind(v),
                    };
                }
                let rows = match q.fetch_all(&self.pool).await {
                    Ok(r) => r,
                    Err(_) => return status(500),
                };
                let mut ids: Vec<i32> = rows.iter().map(|r| r.get::<i32, _>(0)).collect();
                if let Some(t) = &pt {
                    ids.retain(|i| self.allowed(t, p, res.pclass(), Some(*i), "READ"));
                }
                let loaded = match self.load_many(res, &ids).await {
                    Ok(l) => l,
                    Err(_) => return status(500),
                };
                for (k, o) in loaded {
                    let mut v = spec::serialize(k, &o);
                    if let Some(id) = o.get("id").and_then(|i| i.as_i64()) {
                        self.with_url_dups(res, id as i32, &mut v, false).await;
                    }
                    items.push(v);
                }
            }
        }
        json_reply(200, &Value::Array(items), true)
    }

    /// Hibernate's by-id entity loader joins the eagerly fetched collections of the
    /// entity graph in one SQL statement; the `urls` bag of a WMTS source then
    /// repeats once per row of that cartesian product. Returns that row count.
    async fn urls_multiplicity(&self, res: Res, id: i32, by_id: bool) -> i64 {
        let mut m: i64 = 1;
        let mut targets = vec![id];
        if res == Res::Layers {
            // the appearance's properties are joined as well
            if let Ok(Some(r)) = sqlx::query(
                "select count(*) as n from layers l join layerappearances_properties p on p.appearance_id = l.appearance_id where l.id = $1",
            )
            .bind(id)
            .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
            .await
            {
                m *= std::cmp::max(1, r.get::<i64, _>("n"));
            }
        }
        let gkeys: Vec<i32> = match sqlx::query("select grouppermissions_key as k from grouppermissions where entity_id = any($1)")
            .bind(std::mem::take(&mut targets))
            .fetch_all(&self.pool)
            .await
        {
            Ok(rows) => rows.iter().map(|r| r.get::<i32, _>("k")).collect(),
            Err(_) => return m,
        };
        if gkeys.is_empty() {
            return m;
        }
        if !by_id {
            // criteria queries only join the permission entries themselves
            return m * gkeys.len() as i64;
        }
        let rows = sqlx::query(
            "select up.entity_id as g, \
             greatest(1, (select count(*) from permissioncollections_permissions p where p.permissioncollections_id = up.userpermissions_id)) \
             * greatest(1, (select count(*) from users_roles r where r.user_id = up.userpermissions_key)) \
             * greatest(1, (select count(*) from user_usergroup ug where ug.user_id = up.userpermissions_key)) as f \
             from userpermissions up where up.entity_id = any($1)",
        )
        .bind(gkeys.clone())
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await
        .unwrap_or_default();
        let mut sums: HashMap<i32, i64> = HashMap::new();
        for r in rows {
            *sums.entry(r.get::<i32, _>("g")).or_insert(0) += r.get::<i64, _>("f");
        }
        let total: i64 = gkeys.iter().map(|g| sums.get(g).cloned().unwrap_or(1)).sum();
        m * total
    }

    /// Repeat the `urls` of a loaded WMTS source `m` times (see above).
    async fn with_url_dups(&self, res: Res, id: i32, v: &mut Value, by_id: bool) {
        if !Self::has_wmts_urls(res, v) {
            return;
        }
        let m = self.urls_multiplicity(res, id, by_id).await;
        Self::apply_url_dups(res, v, m);
    }

    fn has_wmts_urls(res: Res, v: &Value) -> bool {
        let holder = match res {
            Res::Layers => v.get("source"),
            Res::DataSources => Some(v),
            _ => None,
        };
        match holder {
            Some(h) => h.get("wmtsLayer").is_some() && matches!(h.get("urls"), Some(Value::Array(a)) if !a.is_empty()),
            None => false,
        }
    }

    fn apply_url_dups(res: Res, v: &mut Value, m: i64) {
        let holder: Option<&mut Value> = match res {
            Res::Layers => v.get_mut("source"),
            Res::DataSources => Some(v),
            _ => None,
        };
        let holder = match holder {
            Some(h) if h.get("wmtsLayer").is_some() => h,
            _ => return,
        };
        let urls = match holder.get("urls") {
            Some(Value::Array(a)) if !a.is_empty() => a.clone(),
            _ => return,
        };
        if m > 1 {
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(urls.len() * m as usize);
            for _ in 0..m {
                out.extend(urls.iter().cloned());
            }
            holder["urls"] = Value::Array(out);
        }
    }

    async fn get_one(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, id: i32) -> Reply {
        let loaded = match self.load_one(res, id).await {
            Ok(l) => l,
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        let (kind, obj) = match loaded {
            Some(x) => x,
            None => return status(404),
        };
        if !p.admin {
            let pt = match self.perm_table(p).await {
                Ok(t) => t,
                Err(_) => return status(404),
            };
            if !self.allowed(&pt, p, res.pclass(), Some(id), "READ") {
                return status(404);
            }
        }
        let mut out = spec::serialize(kind, &obj);
        self.with_url_dups(res, id, &mut out, true).await;
        json_reply(200, &out, true)
    }

    async fn create(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, body: &[u8]) -> Reply {
        if res == Res::DataSources {
            return status(400);
        }
        let kind = res.kind();
        let json = match first_json_value(body) {
            Ok(Some(v)) => v,
            _ => return status(400),
        };
        let mut obj = spec::new_instance(kind);
        let mut ctx = DeCtx::default();
        if spec::apply(kind, &mut obj, &json, &mut ctx).is_err() {
            return status(400);
        }
        if obj.get("id").map(|v| !v.is_null()).unwrap_or(false) {
            return status(400);
        }
        for g in &ctx.group_refs {
            if !self.group_exists(*g).await {
                return status(400);
            }
        }
        if !p.admin {
            // a new entity carries no permissions: CREATE is always denied
            return status(400);
        }
        let mut tx = match self.pool.begin().await {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(_) => return status(400),
        };
        let mut sctx = SaveCtx { pool: &self.pool, session_ids: HashSet::new() };
        if store::save(&mut sctx, &mut tx, kind, &mut obj, false).await.is_err() {
            let _ = tx.rollback().await;
            return status(400);
        }
        if tx.commit().await.is_err() {
            return status(400);
        }
        json_reply(201, &spec::serialize(kind, &obj), true)
    }

    async fn update(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, id: i32, body: &[u8]) -> Reply {
        let json = match first_json_value(body) {
            Ok(Some(v)) => v,
            Ok(None) => return status(400),
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        let idv = match json.as_object().and_then(|m| m.get("id")) {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => return status(400),
        };
        if as_int(idv) != id as i64 {
            return status(400);
        }
        let loaded = match self.load_one(res, id).await {
            Ok(Some(l)) => l,
            _ => return status(404),
        };
        let (kind, mut obj) = loaded;
        let pt = if p.admin {
            None
        } else {
            match self.perm_table(p).await {
                Ok(t) => Some(t),
                Err(_) => return status(404),
            }
        };
        if let Some(t) = &pt {
            if !self.allowed(t, p, res.pclass(), Some(id), "READ") || !self.allowed(t, p, res.pclass(), Some(id), "UPDATE") {
                return status(404);
            }
        }
        let url_m = if Self::has_wmts_urls(res, &spec::serialize(kind, &obj)) { self.urls_multiplicity(res, id, true).await } else { 1 };
        let mut session_ids = HashSet::new();
        store::collect_ids(&obj, &mut session_ids);
        // groups referenced by id are resolved with loadById (subject to READ)
        let mut ctx = DeCtx::default();
        let mut wanted: Vec<i64> = vec![];
        if let Some(Value::Array(a)) = json.get("userGroups") {
            for v in a {
                match v {
                    Value::Object(m) => wanted.extend(m.get("id").map(as_int)),
                    other => wanted.push(as_int(other)),
                }
            }
        }
        for g in wanted {
            let g = g as i32;
            let bad = !self.group_exists(g).await
                || match &pt {
                    Some(t) => !self.allowed(t, p, PClass::Group, Some(g), "READ"),
                    None => false,
                };
            if bad {
                ctx.bad_groups.push(g);
            }
        }
        // Jackson applies the properties one by one; when one fails, the
        // earlier ones stay applied and the (checked) exception still commits
        let apply_failed = spec::apply(kind, &mut obj, &json, &mut ctx).is_err();
        let mut tx = match self.pool.begin().await {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        let mut sctx = SaveCtx { pool: &self.pool, session_ids };
        if store::save(&mut sctx, &mut tx, kind, &mut obj, true).await.is_err() {
            let _ = tx.rollback().await;
            return status(404);
        }
        if tx.commit().await.is_err() {
            return status(404);
        }
        if apply_failed {
            return status(404);
        }
        let mut out = spec::serialize(kind, &obj);
        // the loaded (joined) bag keeps its repeated entries unless it was replaced
        if !(res == Res::DataSources && json.get("urls").is_some()) {
            Self::apply_url_dups(res, &mut out, url_m);
        }
        json_reply(200, &out, true)
    }

    async fn group_exists(&self, id: i32) -> bool {
        sqlx::query("select 1 from usergroups where id = $1")
            .bind(id)
            .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
            .await
            .map(|r| r.is_some())
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    async fn remove(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, id: i32) -> Reply {
        let loaded = match self.load_one(res, id).await {
            Ok(Some(l)) => l,
            _ => return status(404),
        };
        let (kind, obj) = loaded;
        if !p.admin {
            let pt = match self.perm_table(p).await {
                Ok(t) => t,
                Err(_) => return status(404),
            };
            if !self.allowed(&pt, p, res.pclass(), Some(id), "READ") || !self.allowed(&pt, p, res.pclass(), Some(id), "DELETE") {
                return status(404);
            }
            if res == Res::Layers {
                // the layer is removed from its maps, which needs UPDATE on them
                let maps = sqlx::query("select distinct map_id from maps_layers where layer_id = $1")
                    .bind(id)
                    .fetch_all(&self.pool)
                    .await;
                match maps {
                    Ok(rows) => {
                        for r in rows {
                            let m: i32 = r.get("map_id");
                            if !self.allowed(&pt, p, PClass::AlwaysRead, Some(m), "UPDATE") {
                                return status(404);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    Err(_) => return status(404),
                }
            }
        }
        let mut tx = match self.pool.begin().await {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        if store::delete(&mut tx, kind, &obj).await.is_err() {
            let _ = tx.rollback().await;
            return status(404);
        }
        if tx.commit().await.is_err() {
            return status(404);
        }
        status(204)
    }

    /// GET /users/{id}/userGroups and GET /groups/{id}/users
    async fn related(&self, res: Res, p: &Principal, id: i32) -> Reply {
        let (target, kind, class) = match res {
            Res::Users => (Res::Groups, Kind::Group, PClass::Group),
            _ => (Res::Users, Kind::User, PClass::User),
        };
        // existence check (the internal findById is not secured)
        let exists = match res {
            Res::Users => sqlx::query("select 1 from users where id = $1").bind(id).fetch_optional(&self.pool).await,
            _ => sqlx::query("select 1 from usergroups where id = $1").bind(id).fetch_optional(&self.pool).await,
        };
        match exists {
            Ok(Some(_)) => {}
            _ => return status(404),
        }
        let rows = match res {
            Res::Users => sqlx::query("select usergroup_id as x from user_usergroup where user_id = $1 order by 1").bind(id).fetch_all(&self.pool).await,
            _ => sqlx::query("select user_id as x from user_usergroup where usergroup_id = $1 order by 1").bind(id).fetch_all(&self.pool).await,
        };
        let mut ids: Vec<i32> = match rows {
            Ok(r) => r.iter().map(|r| r.get::<i32, _>("x")).collect(),
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        if !p.admin {
            let pt = match self.perm_table(p).await {
                Ok(t) => t,
                Err(_) => return status(404),
            };
            ids.retain(|i| self.allowed(&pt, p, class, Some(*i), "READ"));
        }
        let loaded = match self.load_many(target, &ids).await {
            Ok(l) => l,
            Err(_) => return status(404),
        };
        let _ = kind;
        let mut arr: Vec<Value> = loaded.iter().map(|(k, o)| spec::serialize(*k, o)).collect();
        if res == Res::Users && !p.admin {
            // @PostFilter removes the hidden groups from the (shared, in-session)
            // collection of the user, so every embedded copy of that user shows
            // the filtered group ids
            for v in arr.iter_mut() {
                fix_user_groups(v, id, &ids);
            }

    // -------------------------------------------------------------- router

    pub async fn handle(&self, req: Request<Body>) -> Reply {
        let (parts, body) = req.into_parts();
        let path = parts.uri.path().to_string();
        if !(path == "/rest" || path.starts_with("/rest/")) {
            return status(404);
        }
        let (principal, auth) = match self.authenticate(&parts.headers).await {
            Some(x) => x,
            None => return unauthorized(),
        };
        let method = parts.method.clone();
        let query = parse_query(parts.uri.query().unwrap_or(""));
        if path.contains("//") {
            // the original's servlet container answers these with an error page
            return status(500);
        }
        let rest = path.trim_start_matches("/rest").trim_matches('/').to_string();
        let segs: Vec<&str> = if rest.is_empty() { vec![] } else { rest.split('/').collect() };

        // URL security: the six resources need ROLE_USER (or ROLE_ADMIN), the rest ROLE_ADMIN
        let res = segs.first().and_then(|s| Res::from_segment(s));
        let url_ok = if res.is_some() {
            auth.contains(ROLE_USER) || auth.contains(ROLE_ADMIN)
        } else {
            auth.contains(ROLE_ADMIN)
        };
        if !url_ok {
            return status(403);
        }
        let res = match res {
            Some(r) => r,
            None => return status(404),
        };
        let body = match axum::body::to_bytes(body, usize::MAX).await {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(_) => return status(400),
        };
        let p = &principal;
        match segs.len() {
            1 => match method {
                Method::GET => self.list(res, p, &query, false).await,
                Method::POST => self.create(res, p, &body).await,
                _ => method_not_allowed("POST, GET"),
            },
            2 => {
                if segs[1] == "filter" {
                    return match method {
                        Method::GET => self.list(res, p, &query, true).await,
                        Method::PUT | Method::DELETE => status(400),
                        _ => method_not_allowed("GET, PUT, DELETE"),
                    };
                }
                let id: i32 = match segs[1].parse() {
                    Ok(i) => i,
                    Err(_) => {
                        return match method {
                            Method::GET | Method::PUT | Method::DELETE => status(400),
                            _ => method_not_allowed("GET, DELETE, PUT"),
                        }
                    }
                };
                match method {
                    Method::GET => self.get_one(res, p, id).await,
                    Method::PUT => self.update(res, p, id, &body).await,
                    Method::DELETE => self.remove(res, p, id).await,
                    _ => method_not_allowed("GET, DELETE, PUT"),
                }
            }
            3 => {
                let ok = (res == Res::Users && segs[2] == "userGroups") || (res == Res::Groups && segs[2] == "users");
                if !ok {
                    return status(404);
                }
                let id: i32 = match segs[1].parse() {
                    Ok(i) => i,
                    Err(_) => return status(400),
                };
                match method {
                    Method::GET => self.related(res, p, id).await,
                    _ => method_not_allowed("GET"),
                }
            }
            _ => status(404),
        }
    }

//! Java-compatible formatting helpers.

/// `Double.toString(d)`.
pub fn java_double_to_string(d: f64) -> String {
    if d.is_nan() {
        return "NaN".into();
    }
    if d.is_infinite() {
        return if d > 0.0 { "Infinity".into() } else { "-Infinity".into() };
    }
    if d == 0.0 {
        return if d.is_sign_negative() { "-0.0".into() } else { "0.0".into() };
    }
    let sci = format!("{:e}", d.abs()); // e.g. 1.2345e-5
    let (mant, exp) = sci.split_once('e').unwrap();
    let exp: i32 = exp.parse().unwrap();
    let digits: String = mant.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let sign = if d < 0.0 { "-" } else { "" };
    let abs = d.abs();
    if (1e-3..1e7).contains(&abs) {
        // plain decimal notation
        let n = digits.len() as i32;
        let point = exp + 1; // digits before the decimal point
        let s = if point <= 0 {
            format!("0.{}{}", "0".repeat((-point) as usize), digits)
        } else if point >= n {
            format!("{}{}.0", digits, "0".repeat((point - n) as usize))
        } else {
            format!("{}.{}", &digits[..point as usize], &digits[point as usize..])
        };
        format!("{}{}", sign, s)
    } else {
        let first = &digits[..1];
        let rest = if digits.len() > 1 { &digits[1..] } else { "0" };
        format!("{}{}.{}E{}", sign, first, rest, exp)
    }
}

/// Java `toString` of a JSON value as it would appear inside a
/// `Map<String,Object>` (used when persisting appearance properties).
pub fn java_value_to_string(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<String> {
    use serde_json::Value;
    match v {
        Value::Null => None,
        Value::String(s) => Some(s.clone()),
        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),
        Value::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {
                Some(i.to_string())
            } else if let Some(u) = n.as_u64() {
                Some(u.to_string())
            } else {

            }
        }
        Value::Array(a) => Some(format!(
            "[{}]",
            a.iter()
                .map(|x| java_value_to_string(x).unwrap_or_else(|| "null".into()))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        )),
        Value::Object(m) => Some(format!(
            "{{{}}}",
            m.iter()
                .map(|(k, x)| format!("{}={}", k, java_value_to_string(x).unwrap_or_else(|| "null".into())))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        )),
    }

/// The `PropertyValueConverter.convertToEntityAttribute` logic.
pub fn property_from_db(s: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
    use serde_json::json;
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true") {
        return json!(true);
    }
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("false") {
        return json!(false);
    }
    if is_parsable(s) {
        let digits = |t: &str| !t.is_empty() && t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit());
        if digits(s) || (s.starts_with('-') && digits(&s[1..])) {
            if let Ok(l) = s.parse::<i64>() {
                return json!(l);
            }
        } else if let Ok(d) = s.parse::<f64>() {
            return json!(d);
        }
    }
    json!(s)
}

fn is_parsable(s: &str) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() || s.ends_with('.') {
        return false;
    }
    let (body, _) = if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix('-') {
        if rest.is_empty() {
            return false;
        }
        (rest, true)
    } else {
        (s, false)
    };
    let mut points = 0;
    for c in body.chars() {
        if c == '.' {
            points += 1;
            if points > 1 {
                return false;
            }
        } else if !c.is_ascii_digit() {
            return false;
        }
    }
    true
}

pub fn normalize_locale(s: &str) -> String {
    let (lang, country, variant): (String, String, String) = if s.contains('_') {
        let mut it = s.splitn(3, '_');
        let a = it.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let rest = it.collect::<Vec<_>>();
        match rest.len() {
            1 => {
                // "xx_YY" or "xx_YY_VAR" (splitn gave 3 parts max)
                (a, rest[0].to_string(), String::new())
            }
            2 => (a, rest[0].to_string(), rest[1].to_string()),
            _ => (a, String::new(), String::new()),
        }
    } else if s.contains('-') {
        let mut it = s.splitn(3, '-');
        let a = it.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let b = it.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let c = it.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        (a, b, c)
    } else {
        (s.to_string(), String::new(), String::new())
    };
    let lang = lang.to_lowercase();
    let country = country.to_uppercase();
    let mut out = lang.clone();
    if !country.is_empty() || !variant.is_empty() {
        out.push('_');
        out.push_str(&country);
        if !variant.is_empty() {
            out.push('_');
            out.push_str(&variant);
        }
    }
    out
}

fn parse_date(s: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split('-').collect();
    if parts.len() != 3 {
        return None;
    }
    let y: i32 = parts[0].parse().ok()?;
    let m: u32 = parts[1].parse().ok()?;
    let d: u32 = parts[2].parse().ok()?;
    if parts[0].len() < 4
        || parts[1].is_empty()
        || parts[1].len() > 2
        || parts[2].is_empty()
        || parts[2].len() > 2
        || !parts.iter().all(|p| p.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
    {
        return None;
    }
    date_string(y, m, d)
}

fn date_string(y: i32, m: u32, d: u32) -> Option<String> {
    if !(1..=12).contains(&m) || d < 1 {
        return None;
    }
    let leap = (y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || y % 400 == 0;
    let dim = match m {
        1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 12 => 31,
        4 | 6 | 9 | 11 => 30,
        _ => {
            if leap {
                29
            } else {
                28
            }
        }
    };
    if d > dim {
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02}", y, m, d))
}

fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> String {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02}", y, m, d)
}

/// Delete an entity with the rows Hibernate removes along with it.
pub async fn delete(c: &mut PgConnection, kind: Kind, o: &Obj) -> Res<()> {
    let id = gi(o, "id").ok_or_else(|| logic_err("no id"))?;
    let idb = || vec![B::I(Some(id))];
    // permission maps owned by the entity
    exec(c, "delete from userpermissions where entity_id = $1", idb()).await?;
    exec(c, "delete from grouppermissions where entity_id = $1", idb()).await?;
    match kind {
        Kind::User => {
            exec(c, "delete from users_roles where user_id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from user_usergroup where user_id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from users where id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from persons where id = $1", idb()).await?;
        }
        Kind::Group => {
            exec(c, "delete from user_usergroup where usergroup_id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from usergroups_roles where usergroup_id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from usergroups where id = $1", idb()).await?;
        }
        Kind::Role => {
            exec(c, "delete from roles where id = $1", idb()).await?;
        }
        Kind::Layer => {
            let maps: Vec<(i32,)> = sqlx::query_as("select distinct map_id from maps_layers where layer_id = $1")
                .bind(id)
                .fetch_all(&mut *c)
                .await?;
            for (map_id,) in maps {
                let layers: Vec<(i32,)> = sqlx::query_as("select layer_id from maps_layers where map_id = $1 order by idx")
                    .bind(map_id)
                    .fetch_all(&mut *c)
                    .await?;
                exec(c, "delete from maps_layers where map_id = $1", vec![B::I(Some(map_id))]).await?;
                let mut idx = 0;
                for (l,) in layers {
                    if l == id {
                        continue;
                    }
                    exec(
                        c,
                        "insert into maps_layers (map_id, layer_id, idx) values ($1, $2, $3)",
                        vec![B::I(Some(map_id)), B::I(Some(l)), B::I(Some(idx))],
                    )
                    .await?;
                    idx += 1;
                }
            }
            exec(c, "delete from layers where id = $1", idb()).await?;
        }
        Kind::Appearance => {
            exec(c, "delete from layerappearances_properties where appearance_id = $1", idb()).await?;
            exec(c, "delete from layerappearances where id = $1", idb()).await?;
        }
        Kind::DsImage | Kind::DsTile | Kind::DsWfs | Kind::DsWmts | Kind::DsXyz => {
            let mut cascade_tilegrid = None;
            match kind {
                Kind::DsTile => {
                    exec(c, "delete from tilewmslayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                    exec(c, "delete from imagewmslayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                }
                Kind::DsImage => {
                    exec(c, "delete from imagewmslayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                }
                Kind::DsWfs => {
                    exec(c, "delete from wfslayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                }
                Kind::DsWmts => {
                    exec(c, "delete from wmtslayerdatasources_urls where wmtslayerdatasources_id = $1", idb()).await?;
                    exec(c, "delete from wmtslayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                    if let Some(Value::Object(t)) = o.get("tileGrid") {
                        cascade_tilegrid = gi(t, "id");
                    }
                }
                Kind::DsXyz => {
                    exec(c, "delete from xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution where xyzlayerdatasrc_id = $1", idb()).await?;
                    exec(c, "delete from xyzlayerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            exec(c, "delete from layerdatasources where id = $1", idb()).await?;
            if let Some(t) = cascade_tilegrid {
                // CascadeType.ALL on WmtsLayerDataSource.tileGrid
                let tb = || vec![B::I(Some(t))];
                exec(c, "delete from userpermissions where entity_id = $1", tb()).await?;
                exec(c, "delete from grouppermissions where entity_id = $1", tb()).await?;
                exec(c, "delete from wmtstilegrids_matrixids where wmtstilegrids_id = $1", tb()).await?;
                exec(c, "delete from tilegrid_resolution where tilegrid_id = $1", tb()).await?;
                exec(c, "delete from wmtstilegrids where id = $1", tb()).await?;
                exec(c, "delete from tilegrids where id = $1", tb()).await?;
            }
        }
        Kind::Extent | Kind::TileGrid | Kind::WmtsTileGrid => return Err(logic_err("not supported")),
    }
    Ok(())
}
